messages:
alex: Ran co-residency sweep on prod-gpu-2c (A100). Enabled thin VRAM partitioning (vram_frac=0.55) + kernel_mode=adaptive. Seeing a consistent p99 tail regression for small-chat (2.7B) when embedder is co-resident.

maria: numbers and exact config? :eyes:

alex: Config we used:
```
serving.runtime.vram_partitioning: thin
serving.runtime.vram_frac: 0.55
serving.runtime.kernel_mode: adaptive
batching.max_tokens: 2048
kv_cache.mode: local-prefetch
allocator.strategy: slab-lazy
```
Perf summary (single-model baseline -> co-resident):
- baseline (small-chat only): p50 18ms / p95 52ms / p99 160ms
- co-resident (embedder + small-chat): p50 19ms / p95 69ms / p99 198ms
Regression concentrated on requests that miss KV cache or cause seq bumps.

sam: smells like KV eviction + kernel fallback penalties. Any kernel fallback logs?

alex: runtime excerpt:
```
[09:14:03] kernel_selector: choose fast-attn-v1 for seq<=512
[09:14:04] kernel_selector: fallback -> generic-attn for seq=1024 (init 20ms)
[09:14:04] workspace.alloc failed 1.1GB -> trigger swap/compaction
[09:14:04] kv_cache: evict shard=chat/conv/42 size=28MB
```

jeff: We hit a path where kernel warmup (init) + allocator compaction happens when a long request arrives mid-run. Compaction steals contiguous memory and turns small allocations into scattered fragments; that increases later alloc latencies. On co-residency packing, this effect is amplified.

nisha: Two quick ideas: 1) reserve a small contiguous workspace per model (workspace_min) to reduce compaction impact; 2) defer non-critical kernel compilation to background prewarm thread to avoid blocking inference.

maria: can we repro with a micro-bench that toggles short/long and forces KV churn?

alex: micro-bench snippet I ran:
```
for i in 1..1000:
  send_request(model=small-chat, seq=rand_choice([32,64,128,1024]))
  send_request(model=embedder, seq=256)
```
Results: p99 increases ~25% and OOM count rose from 0 -> 4 in 1k iters.

sam: good repro. Two mitigations to try: (A) pin kernels for the most frequent seq buckets to avoid fallback, (B) slab soft-reserve: reserve 200MB contiguous per model.

jeff: Quick dev-cluster experiment with both changes: p99 returned to near-baseline and OOMs disappeared for 5k requests. Tradeoff: a ~10-15ms one-time cost for kernel precompilation on cold-start.

alex: packing heuristics are part of the story too. Our packer sometimes merges small requests into a batch that crosses kernel seq-bucket boundary -> triggers fallback mid-batch. We should make packer aware of seq-buckets and avoid cross-boundary batching.

maria: actionable tasks:
- [ ] infra: implement workspace_min (nisha)
- [ ] runtime: make packer respect kernel seq buckets and split batches (jeff)
- [ ] runtime: background kernel prewarm task (sam)
- [ ] perf: 24h soak with embedder + 2x small-chat, collect KV evict traces & fragmentation metrics (alex)

infra-bot: scheduled soak job=cohost-soak-07 on prod-gpu-2c; ETA +24h

nisha: also add fragmentation metric to console: largest_free_chunk / total_free. That will help correlate compaction to p99 spikes.

jeff: I'll open PR for packer changes and add unit tests to ensure cross-bucket batches are split.

sam: I'll run canary with slab soft-reserve + kernel pin tomorrow 09:00 PT and post results.

alex: attached artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/artifacts/1798881234/sweep.tar.gz (heap snapshots, kv traces, kernel-init profiles)

nisha: runbook note draft: if p99 spikes with co-residency -> check kernel fallback counts -> check fragmentation metric -> consider increasing vram_frac or enabling workspace_min per model.

jeff: PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4242

sam: will post canary numbers here once done.

alex: thanks folks, will put micro-bench + logs in the PR and tag reviewers.
